paras.en: To help them do this, they filmed in the original New Jersey woods where the first film was shot.
paras.zh: 为了帮助他们做到这一点，他们在第一部电影拍摄的新泽西州原始树林中进行了拍摄。

paras.en: “There are no woods and no trees and no leaves that look like Jersey woods trees and leaves, so we had to go back to the OG to to Blairstown, New Jersey, the original town, which is amazing,” said Kane. “It was very welcoming and hasn’t changed a day in 45 years.”
paras.zh: “没有树林，没有树木，也没有叶子，看起来像泽西森林的树木和叶子，所以我们不得不回到 OG 去新泽西州的布莱尔斯敦，原来的小镇，这太棒了，”凯恩说。 “这里非常热情，45 年来从未改变过。”

paras.en: In those woods and at that summer camp, Camp Crystal will tap into the novelization of part two. “We go pretty deep on Jason’s background, Jason in the woods crawling out of the lake, and all that stuff. But it’s a little bit invention too,” the series creator shared. “For me, Pamela talks about her relationship with Jason and how much she meant to him, and we see the person that she is in the first movie, but we don’t really see the cornerstone of that relationship. We don’t really see her and Jason as people before all that stuff happened. She wasn’t born a psychopath, but there was a journey that took her from a loving and protective mother to the person we know in the first movie, and I wanted to show that.”
paras.zh: 在那些树林里和那个夏令营中，水晶营将利用第二部分的小说。 “我们对杰森的背景进行了相当深入的研究，杰森在树林里从湖里爬出来，等等。但这也有点发明，”该剧的创作者分享道。 “对我来说，帕梅拉谈论了她与杰森的关系以及她对他的意义，我们在第一部电影中看到了她，但我们并没有真正看到这种关系的基石。在所有这些事情发生之前，我们并没有真正将她和杰森视为人。她并不是生来就是一个精神病患者，但有一段旅程将她从一个充满爱心和保护性的母亲变成了我们在第一部电影中认识的人，我想展示这一点。”

paras.en: The series also wanted to show the real Jason as a child, which meant putting a young Vinson into a 13-pound prosthetic head. “Linda got very protective of Calum with that, too. It was like, get that thing off his head now. He’s too hot. You’re burning his brain.”
paras.zh: 该剧还想展现真实的杰森小时候，这意味着要给年轻的文森戴上 13 磅重的假头。 “琳达对此也非常保护卡勒姆。就好像，现在把那东西从他头上拿下来。他太热了。你正在烧伤他的大脑。”

paras.en: As a series focused on building the origins of the Friday the 13th story, Crystal Lake will feature both original, entirely new, as well as established characters from the films. Among the returning are Dorf (Cameron Scoggins) and Ralph Neeley (Nick Cordileone). In terms of how fans will see them in the series, “What Brad did, what the writing team did, was take this thing that’s a trope for horror films… and fleshed it out in a way where you go, ‘Well, who is he? Why is he this way? What’s he warning people about? Where is he coming from?’” Cordileone said. “It was an absolute gift to just come and be able to live that. He’s an unreliable narrator too. But he’s very positive about some things. It’s a real tug of war.
paras.zh: 作为一个专注于构建《十三号星期五》故事起源的系列剧，《水晶湖》将以电影中的原创、全新和既定角色为特色。回归者包括多尔夫（卡梅伦·斯科金斯饰）和拉尔夫·尼利（尼克·科迪莱昂饰）。至于粉丝们在剧中的看法，“布拉德所做的，编剧团队所做的，就是采用了恐怖电影的比喻……并以一种让你想到的方式充实它，‘好吧，他是谁？他为什么这样？他在警告人们什么？他来自哪里？’”科迪莱昂说。 “来到这里并能够经历这样的生活绝对是一份礼物。他也是一个不可靠的叙述者。但他对某些事情非常积极。这是一场真正的拉锯战。

paras.en: “We really calibrated on set as we went in terms of the characters from the movie versus the characters we’re doing here. Cameron and Nick, sometimes asked me, ‘How Crazy Ralph do you want me to go here? How do you want me to Dorf out?’” added Kane. “Sometimes Nick would put on this beautiful heartfelt performance, and I’d go get him between the takes, and just go, ‘Just do the voice, just do the crazy,’ and he would do it. The same thing with Cameron, you know, go full Dorf out, and he would do it, for better or worse.”
paras.zh: “当我们根据电影中的角色与我们在这里扮演的角色进行拍摄时，我们确实在片场进行了校准。卡梅伦和尼克有时会问我，‘你想让我怎么去这里？你想让我怎么把多尔夫带出去？’”凯恩补充道。 “有时尼克会表演这种美丽而真诚的表演，我会在拍摄间隙让他这么做，然后说，‘只要做声音，做疯狂的事情’，他就会这么做。卡梅隆也是一样，你知道，让多尔夫全力以赴，他就会这么做，无论好坏。”

articles.title: Jessica Lange, Sarah Paulson and the ‘Coven’ on What Brought Them Back to ‘American Horror Story’ — and If This Is the End
articles.author: Jackie Strause

paras.en: [This story contains spoilers from episodes seven and eight of American Horror Story season 13, “The Baddest Witch Of Them All” and “Hell No.”]
paras.zh: [本故事包含《美国恐怖故事》第 13 季第七集和第八集《最坏女巫》和《地狱号》的剧透]

paras.en: No one in American Horror Story ever really dies… and that’s part of the appeal to returning to the veteran horror franchise for the witches who make up the Coven.
paras.zh: 《美国恐怖故事》中没有人真正死去……这也是组成女巫集会的女巫重返老牌恐怖系列的吸引力之一。

paras.en: Picking up from a cliffhanger for Sarah Paulson‘s Supreme witch, Cordelia Goode — seemingly dead from an axe to the head from Evan Peters’ James Patrick March — the seventh episode of the all-star crossover 13th season brought Cordelia back to life in a resurrection scene that marked the long-awaited return of the all-time Supreme — Cordelia’s mother, Fiona Goode, played by Jessica Lange.
paras.zh: 莎拉·保尔森 (Sarah Paulson) 饰演的至尊女巫科迪莉亚·古德 (Cordelia Goode) 似乎被埃文·彼得斯 (Evan Peters) 饰演的詹姆斯·帕特里克·马奇 (James Patrick March) 的斧头劈中头部而死，在这部全明星跨界剧第 13 季的第七集中，科迪莉亚在复活场景中复活，这标志着人们期待已久的至尊女巫科迪莉亚·古德 (由杰西卡·兰格饰演) 的母亲菲奥娜·古德 (Fiona Goode) 回归。

paras.en: The mother-daughter reunion brought the arrival of Lange’s third iconic franchise character (Sister Jude is still waiting in the wings), and set up the Coven witches as the women tasked with saving the world in a season that brings major villains back from the dead, and many actors back to the franchise.
paras.zh: 母女重聚带来了兰格的第三个标志性系列角色（裘德修女仍在等待）的到来，并让女巫集会女巫成为肩负拯救世界任务的女性，这一季让主要恶棍起死回生，许多演员也回到了系列。

paras.en: The Hollywood Reporter spoke to the coven — Lange, Paulson, Billie Lourd, Gabourey Sidibe and Leslie Grossman — who all say they were easily lured back to the franchise by mastermind Ryan Murphy, and that they were led to believe season 13 could be the last of the franchise. Trick’s on them, however — as Murphy now says he’d like to do the franchise “forever.”
paras.zh: 《好莱坞报道》采访了兰格、保尔森、比莉·洛德、加布蕾·西迪贝和莱斯利·格罗斯曼等成员，他们都表示，他们很容易被策划者瑞安·墨菲引诱回到该系列，并且他们被引导相信第 13 季可能是该系列的最后一季。然而，他们已经被戏弄了——墨菲现在说他想“永远”经营这个系列。

paras.en: Will season 13 close the Coven chapter, or set their characters up for more AHS? They may not all be on the same page about that (we’re looking at you, Lady Lange), but below, the close-knit ensemble dives in about what drew them back, what it’s like to return to these fan-favorite characters and the magic of the megahit horror series. “It was like a return to something that had been the beginning,” says Lange.
paras.zh: 第 13 季会结束《女巫集会》一章，还是让他们的角色为更多《美国恐怖故事》做好准备？他们可能对此看法不一（兰格女士，我们正在看你），但下面，这个紧密团结的团队深入探讨了是什么吸引了他们，回归这些粉丝最喜欢的角色是什么感觉，以及这部热门恐怖系列的魔力。 “这就像回到了最初的起点，”兰格说。

paras.en: At the beginning of this season, Ryan Murphy told me you all quickly said yes when he called to ask if you would return for season 13. He said he started with you, Jessica, and that if you had said no, he probably would not have done this all-star season at all. I know you had a condition — to play all four of your AHS characters. Can you talk about why you came back after all these years? (Note: Lange last played a series regular in season four, and guest starred in season eight.)
paras.zh: 在本赛季开始时，瑞安·墨菲告诉我，当他打电话询问你们是否会回归第 13 季时，你们很快就答应了。他说他从你开始，杰西卡，如果你拒绝，他可能根本不会参加这个全明星赛季。我知道你有一个条件——扮演《美国恐怖故事》中的所有四个角色。能谈谈为什么这么多年后才回来吗？ （注：兰格最后一次在第四季中担任常规角色，并在第八季中客串出演。）

paras.en: JESSICA LANGE (Laughs.) I’ll preface this by saying that when Ryan wants something, he is the most seductive. He can usually talk you into just about anything.
paras.zh: 杰西卡·兰格（笑）。我会在序言中说，当瑞安想要某样东西时，他是最有诱惑力的。他通常可以说服你做任何事情。

paras.en: But when he approached me about this, he was interested, of course, in the character of Constance [from Murder House], because I think, of the four characters I’ve played, Constance was perhaps his favorite. But I said I would consider doing it if I could play all four of the characters that I had established on the show in those first four seasons, because then I was basically done with [the show].
paras.zh: 但当他向我询问此事时，他当然对康斯坦斯（来自《谋杀屋》）这个角色感兴趣，因为我认为，在我扮演的四个角色中，康斯坦斯可能是他最喜欢的。但我说，如果我能扮演我在前四个赛季中在节目中建立的所有四个角色，我会考虑这样做，因为那时我基本上就完成了[节目]。

paras.en: So [I asked about] the four characters, he said yes, and it kind of went from there. And then knowing I’d be working with the same company of people — Sarah and Gabby and Billy, all of us — and Evan [Peters]. It became interesting, because it was like a return to something that had been the beginning. So that was it. Hopefully we’d get some good scenes, some good writing and directing. That was the genesis for me.
paras.zh: 所以[我问起]这四个角色，他说是的，然后事情就从那里开始了。然后我知道我将与同一群人一起工作——莎拉、加比和比利，我们所有人——还有埃文（彼得斯）。这变得很有趣，因为这就像回到了最初的地方。就是这样。希望我们能得到一些好的场景、好的编剧和导演。这就是我的起源。

paras.en: Sarah, you had taken time away from American Horror Story, and now you come back playing five (so far) of your characters. Did you have to think about coming back? And were these additional parts [Ms. Venable, Hypodermic Sally, Mamie Eisenhower and Tuberculosis Karen] an easy, “Yes, yes, yes, yes”?
paras.zh: 莎拉，你离开了《美国恐怖故事》一段时间，现在你回来扮演五个（到目前为止）角色。你有必要考虑回来吗？这些额外的部分是[女士]吗？ Venable、皮下注射莎莉、玛米·艾森豪威尔和结核病凯伦]一个简单的“是的，是的，是的，是的”？

paras.en: SARAH PAULSON I had had enough of a break that the impulse was to say yes, but then Ryan said, “Jessica’s back,” and I said, “Well, then I’m doing it.” It was really pretty simple.
paras.zh: 莎拉·保尔森（SARAH PAULSON） 我已经休息够了，所以有冲动说“是”，但后来瑞安说，“杰西卡回来了，”我说，“好吧，那我就这么做了。”这真的很简单。

paras.en: Not to sully the names of all the other wonderful people who were part of the show. I stood, I think, three seasons down…
paras.zh: 不要玷污节目中所有其他精彩人物的名字。我想，我站了三个赛季……

paras.en: PAULSON And I wasn’t in NYC, and I wasn’t in Delicate. There were three seasons I didn’t do it at all, so it had been a very long time. Jessica hadn’t been back since season [four as a series regular but since season] eight, actually, because remember I directed you in that episode?
paras.zh: 保尔森：我不在纽约，也不在精致。有三个赛季我根本没有这样做，所以已经很长一段时间了。事实上，杰西卡自第四季以来就没有回来过（作为系列常规演员，但自第八季以来），因为还记得那一集是我导演的吗？

paras.en: LANGE Oh, yes, for the return to Murder House [in Apocalypse].
paras.zh: 兰格：哦，是的，为了重返谋杀屋（《启示录》）。

paras.en: PAULSON So there had been a little bit of that, but we had all not been together as the OG group in so long that when Ryan said that was his plan, I just said, “Well, that sounds too delicious and fun.” He didn’t promise me I would get to play any characters, but… I got to do a few.
paras.zh: PAULSON 所以确实有一些这样的事情，但我们作为 OG 团队已经很久没有在一起了，所以当 Ryan 说这是他的计划时，我只是说，“嗯，这听起来太美味太有趣了。”他没有向我保证我会扮演任何角色，但是……我必须扮演一些角色。

paras.en: And I didn’t get to do them enough. I play some of those for literally 20 seconds — jumping into the hell mouth [in episode four].
paras.zh: 而且我做得还不够。其中一些我玩了 20 秒——跳进地狱之口（第四集）。

paras.en: Fans are calling for more Tuberculosis Karen [from Double Feature].
paras.zh: 粉丝们呼吁更多结核病凯伦[来自双重特征]。

paras.en: PAULSON (Laughs.) Yeah, Tuberculosis Karen is great. I would have liked to have done more of that.
paras.zh: 保尔森（笑）是的，结核病凯伦很棒。我本来希望做得更多。

paras.en: Yes, I’d love you to ask you how Ryan convinced you to play Margaret Thatcher in that same “Jezebel’s Ball” sacrifice scene — or was that your idea?
paras.zh: 是的，我很想问你瑞安是如何说服你在“耶洗别舞会”牺牲场景中扮演玛格丽特·撒切尔的——或者这是你的主意？

paras.en: LANGE That was my idea, because I figured if you’re throwing 13 women who have been guilty of horrendous things, that you couldn’t do that without Margaret Thatcher.
paras.zh: 兰格：那是我的想法，因为我想，如果你要抛弃 13 名犯有可怕罪行的女性，那么如果没有玛格丽特·撒切尔，你就无法做到这一点。

paras.en: Billie, you also play two characters this season. Did you know that going in?
paras.zh: 比莉，你这一季也扮演两个角色。你知道进去吗？

paras.en: BILLIE LOURD I did. That was part of Ryan’s pitch to me too, is that I got to play two of my favorite characters. I wish I would have gotten to play Montana [from 1984], ’cause she’s my fave. But now I’ve had two kids, and I wouldn’t really fit in the little aerobics suit anymore, so I’m kind of happy I didn’t play her! But I got to play Winter and Mallory. Sweet, poor Mallory, the poor girl in every scene is just so sad. It’s really tough for me.
paras.zh: 比莉·洛德 我做到了。这也是瑞安向我推销的一部分，那就是我必须扮演两个我最喜欢的角色。我希望我能扮演蒙大拿（1984 年起），因为她是我的最爱。但现在我已经有了两个孩子，我已经不再适合穿小健美操服了，所以我很高兴我没有玩她！但我必须扮演温特和马洛里。可爱的，可怜的马洛里，每个场景中那个可怜的女孩都是那么悲伤。这对我来说真的很难。

paras.en: But it was great. I’d never gotten to play two characters in one show and that was really gratifying and such a fun thing to do as an actress, even though I didn’t get to play Winter for that long.
paras.zh: 但这很棒。我从来没有在一场演出中扮演两个角色，作为一名演员，这真的很令人欣慰，也是一件很有趣的事情，尽管我没能扮演冬天那么久。

paras.en: PAULSON Yeah, that was a brief one. Season 14… [invoking Game of Thrones] Winter is back!
paras.zh: 保尔森：是的，那是一个简短的故事。第 14 季……[援引《权力的游戏》] 冬天回来了！

paras.en: LANGE I want to also say that Ryan said this was the last season. But now I understand that perhaps, it’s not.
paras.zh: 兰格 我还想说瑞安说这是最后一季了。但现在我明白了，也许，事实并非如此。

paras.en: Was that you’re understanding going into this season, that season 13 would be the last for AHS? Because in speaking to Ryan since, he has told us he wants to keep doing AHS “forever” (just not necessarily as big and all-starry as season 13).
paras.zh: 您是否理解进入本季时，第 13 季将是《美国恐怖故事》的最后一季？因为从那以后与 Ryan 交谈时，他告诉我们他想“永远”继续制作《美国恐怖故事》（只是不一定像第 13 季那样规模宏大、明星荟萃）。

paras.en: PAULSON I don’t know, but I thought it was the last one, too.
paras.zh: 保尔森：我不知道，但我认为这也是最后一次。

paras.en: GROSSMAN I think it’s understood that the show is going to go as long as he would like to keep doing the show. I was not under the same impression. I feel like he said it, though.
paras.zh: 格罗斯曼：我认为只要他愿意继续做这个节目，这个节目就会继续下去，这是可以理解的。我却没有同样的印象。不过我感觉是他说的。

paras.en: PAULSON Ryan, what the hell were you thinking? (Laughs.)
paras.zh: 保尔森 瑞安，你到底在想什么？ （笑）

paras.en: LOURD I think it was said quickly, and then taken away.
paras.zh: 劳德：我认为这句话说得很快，然后就被拿走了。

paras.en: LOURD Then I really won’t fit in the aerobics costume. (Laughs.)
paras.zh: 洛德：那我真的不适合穿健美操服装了。 （笑）

paras.en: Ryan also said that when you all came back to set, as soon as each of you landed your accents, it was like no time had passed. Leslie and Gabourey, is that how you felt? That once you found your characters’ voices, it was like you never left?
paras.zh: 瑞安还说，当你们回到片场时，一旦你们每个人都说出了自己的口音，就好像时间没有过去一样。莱斯利和加布蕾，你们也是这么想的吗？一旦你找到了角色的声音，就好像你从未离开过？

paras.en: SIDIBE I think there’s a quiet anger to Queenie and the second I like unlock that, the quiet anger in myself, I was pretty much back.
paras.zh: 西迪贝：我认为奎妮有一种安静的愤怒，当我想释放它时，我内心的安静愤怒，我几乎回来了。

paras.en: GROSSMAN For me, it’s more about getting to be with the people I had gotten to be with before, that there is a connection and a comfort with, and that gets you right back into the mode. I love working with everyone. I really love my scenes with Gabby. I always feel like there’s a Lucy and Ethel vibe [from I Love Lucy] that goes on between us every time, and you see that in episode seven. Obviously, these are people who mean a great deal to me, and when we get together, there is an alchemy and a vibe and a feeling that gets you right back into it.
paras.zh: 格罗斯曼：对我来说，更重要的是与我以前交往过的人在一起，建立联系并感到舒适，这会让你立即回到原来的模式。我喜欢和大家一起工作。我真的很喜欢和嘉比在一起的场景。我总觉得我们之间每次都会出现露西和埃塞尔的氛围（《我爱露西》），你在第七集中就看到了这一点。显然，这些人对我来说意义重大，当我们聚在一起时，就会有一种魔力、一种氛围和一种让你重新融入其中的感觉。

paras.en: I am obsessed with Coco’s gluten powers.
paras.zh: 我对可可的麸质力量很着迷。

paras.en: GROSSMAN Look, she started off as a gluten detector, and now she’s able to kick a little ass. And you know what? Thank God. Jessica, you have no idea. [Note: They haven’t yet been in scenes together.] You don’t know the power that Coco has!
paras.zh: 格罗斯曼：瞧，她一开始是一名麸质检测员，现在她已经能干得漂亮了。你知道吗？感谢上帝。杰西卡，你不知道。 【注：他们还没有一起拍戏。】你不知道可可的力量！

paras.en: GROSSMAN Thankfully, Coco was elevated, and has gotten to kick a little more ass.
paras.zh: 格罗斯曼 值得庆幸的是，可可的地位得到了提升，并且能够踢更多的屁股。

paras.en: Sarah, Cordelia’s fate was a big cliffhanger last week, and we now know she is resurrected by her mother, marking Jessica’s return as our first Supreme, Fiona. Did you all know the whole arc going into the season, or were you finding out as you got scripts?
paras.zh: 莎拉·科迪莉亚的命运上周是一个悬念，我们现在知道她被她的母亲复活了，这标志着杰西卡作为我们第一位至尊菲奥娜的回归。你们都知道这一季的整个剧情吗，还是在拿到剧本时才知道的？

paras.en: PAULSON I don’t think they [the writers] knew the whole arc going in. (Laughs.) They were figuring it out.
paras.zh: 保尔森：我认为他们（编剧们）不知道整个情节。（笑）他们正在弄清楚。

paras.en: LANGE You never knew from one moment to another what your character was going to do.
paras.zh: 兰格：你永远不知道你的角色会做什么。

paras.en: PAULSON We were we were all kind of flying blind.
paras.zh: 保尔森 我们当时都是盲目的。

paras.en: LANGE But that was the way we always were. You were lucky if you got the scene the morning of.
paras.zh: 兰格 但我们一直都是这样。如果你早上能看到这个场景，那你就很幸运了。

paras.en: PAULSON I think it’s a real testament. Anytime you see somebody on television doing good work, you have to recognize that there is sometimes an upwards of nine to 10 pages that are being done in a day. Whereas if you do a film, you’re doing a page and a half, maybe two pages? The output is voluminous. So for actors who are able to do it and to do it quickly and to think quickly, it’s pretty amazing. That’s what this crew of people can do.
paras.zh: 保尔森：我认为这是一个真正的证明。每当您在电视上看到某人做得很好时，您都必须认识到有时一天内完成了九到十页以上的工作。但如果你拍一部电影，你会拍一页半，甚至两页？输出量很大。所以对于那些能够做到这一点，而且做得很快，思考也很快的演员来说，这是非常了不起的。这就是这群人能做的。

paras.en: I have been told the Coven remains very relevant throughout the entire season.
paras.zh: 我被告知女巫集会在整个赛季中仍然非常重要。

paras.en: This eighth episode certainly sets them up to be the saviors of the world. Your fellow witch, Emma Roberts, said that the ending closes a chapter. Is that how you all felt, like the closing of a chapter?
paras.zh: 第八集无疑让他们成为世界的救世主。你的女巫同伴艾玛·罗伯茨说，结局结束了一个章节。这就是你们大家的感受吗，就像一章的结束？

paras.en: SIDIBE Oh, absolutely not. Honestly, that last episode, I said, “We’ll be here in six months.”
paras.zh: 西迪贝 哦，绝对不是。老实说，在最后一集，我说，“我们将在六个月内到达这里。”

paras.en: SIDIBE Sure, some chapters close, but the full book is still the full book.
paras.zh: 西迪贝 当然，有些章节已经结束，但整本书仍然是整本书。

paras.en: PAULSON I think you’re probably right about that.
paras.zh: 保尔森：我认为你的说法可能是对的。

paras.en: LANGE [to Paulson] You’re going back for Coven again?
paras.zh: 兰格（对保尔森）你又要回到科文了吗？

paras.en: PAULSON No one’s called me about anything. I know nothing about it, but it is the story that I always feel like I would like to go back to. I would like to go back in time and have Salem witches to talk about the origins of how we found ourselves the coven that we are today, I would be interested in that. But what I like doesn’t necessarily mean that’s what he’s [Murphy] going to be interested in telling.
paras.zh: 保尔森：没有人给我打电话询问任何事情。我对此一无所知，但这是我总觉得我想回去的故事。我想回到过去，让塞勒姆女巫们谈谈我们如何找到今天的女巫集会的起源，我对此很感兴趣。但我喜欢的内容并不一定意味着他（墨菲）有兴趣讲述的内容。

paras.en: Would it interest all of you to come back to Coven again quickly, or was it appealing to have some time away?
paras.zh: 你们所有人是否有兴趣尽快再次回到女巫集会，或者离开一段时间是否很有吸引力？

paras.en: PAULSON Well, now that we’re here, I’m just like… We haven’t done Coven since [season eight] Apocalypse, so it’s been like five years or something.
paras.zh: 保尔森：好吧，既然我们在这里，我就想……自《天启》第八季以来我们就没有做过《女巫集会》了，所以已经有五年了。

paras.en: Jessica, would you leave the door open to return again, or is this a one-and-done for you?
paras.zh: 杰西卡，你会敞开大门再次回来吗？还是这对你来说是一劳永逸的事情？

paras.en: LANGE This is a one and done, I think, yeah. I got to play those four characters, I enjoyed it. Got to work with this ensemble of actors again, which was wonderful. But no, there’s no reason to. I wasn’t interested in creating a new storyline or a new character, really.
paras.zh: LANGE 这是一件已经完成的事情，我想，是的。我必须扮演这四个角色，我很享受。再次与这群演员合作，真是太棒了。但不，没有理由这样做。我真的对创造新的故事情节或新的角色不感兴趣。

paras.en: PAULSON I’m just gonna put it out there — that I’ve seen many an interview with Jessica on the streets of New York, where she’s being accosted by a fan, and they ask whether she’s going to come back, and she’s like, “Absolutely not.” And yet, here we are. So I’m just saying… (laughs.)
paras.zh: 保尔森：我只想说出来——我在纽约街头见过很多杰西卡的采访，她被粉丝搭讪，他们问她是否会回来，她的回答是：“绝对不会。”然而，我们到了。所以我只是说……（笑）

paras.en: LANGE But no, no, no. This was an extraordinary [season]… this was a different thing. This was revisiting four characters and weaving them together. That was fun, but you can’t keep doing that forever.
paras.zh: 兰格 但是不，不，不。这是一个非凡的[季节]……这是一件不同的事情。这是重新审视四个角色并将它们编织在一起。这很有趣，但你不能永远这样做。

paras.en: PAULSON You would watch! I mean, I think if the appetite is there for the people…
paras.zh: 保尔森 你会看的！我的意思是，我认为如果人们有胃口……

paras.en: Ryan did tell me, Jessica, that you had shared when you were doing Broadway, that fans were approaching you about American Horror Story, and that touched or motivated you to want to return. Are you all still amazed at the AHS fandom and how much it resonates?
paras.zh: 瑞安确实告诉我，杰西卡，你在百老汇演出时分享过，粉丝们向你询问《美国恐怖故事》，这触动或激励你想要回归。你们还对《美国恐怖故事》的粉丝群体及其引起的共鸣感到惊讶吗？

paras.en: LANGE Well, it’s always different when someone comes up to you on the street. You never know what it is about your work and your history of work that has touched them or that they’re going to speak about. For young people, a lot of times it is American Horror Story. It’s not always; it really depends on who’s seen what. It’s always interesting to me.
paras.zh: 兰格：嗯，当有人在街上向你走来时，情况总是不同的。你永远不知道你的工作和工作历史的哪些内容触动了他们，或者他们会谈论什么。对于年轻人来说，很多时候就是美国恐怖故事。并不总是如此；这实际上取决于谁看到了什么。这对我来说总是很有趣。

paras.en: PAULSON What about you, Gabby? Do people come up to you all the time for Queenie?
paras.zh: 保尔森 你呢，加比？人们总是来找你找奎妮吗？

paras.en: SIDIBE It’s a lot of Queenie. But also, it’s a lot of Precious. It’s Difficult People. But I think the most aggressive fanbase is absolutely American Horror Story (laughs), 100 percent.
paras.zh: 西迪贝 这是很多奎妮。而且，它也很珍贵。这是很难相处的人。但我认为最激进的粉丝群绝对是《美国恐怖故事》（笑），100%。

paras.en: GROSSMAN It is incredible how fervent the fanbase is and how Ryan has been able to keep this show very much in the zeitgeist for 13 seasons.
paras.zh: 格罗斯曼 令人难以置信的是，粉丝群的热情如此之高，瑞安如何能够让这部剧在 13 季中始终保持时代精神。

paras.en: PAULSON What other show is really doing that? Constantly reinventing itself and using the same company of actors? I remember in the beginning, when it went from Murder House to Asylum, the fans were like, “Wait, Evan is Tate. He cannot be Kit.” It was really unnerving for them at first and now, I feel like they expect it They’re kind of in on it. They want to see what everybody’s going to do and what the new characters are, and that makes it feel sort of interactive with the audience in a way that’s very cool, because they are looking forward to seeing what the actors are going to do.
paras.zh: 保尔森 还有哪个节目真正做到了这一点？不断重塑自我并使用同一家演员公司？我记得一开始，当它从谋杀屋到庇护所时，粉丝们就像是，“等等，埃文是泰特。他不可能是基特。”起初这真的让他们感到不安，但现在，我觉得他们对此有所期待，他们有点参与其中。他们想看看每个人都会做什么以及新角色是什么，这使得与观众的互动感觉非常酷，因为他们期待看到演员们会做什么。

paras.en: Jessica, you’re reprising another one of your characters in the film adaptation of Long Day’s Journey Into Night, and I wanted to ask all of you, what appeals to you at this point in your careers? Is it TV, film, the stage? In this case, it seems like it was about revisiting characters you all loved.
paras.zh: 杰西卡，你将在电影《漫漫长夜之旅》中再次扮演你的另一个角色，我想问你们所有人，在你们职业生涯的这个阶段，什么对你们有吸引力？是电视、电影、舞台吗？在这种情况下，这似乎是关于重温你们都喜欢的角色。

paras.en: LANGE Well, I mean, it’s all of those, depending on the role, depending on the company, depending on so many things, but I love doing stage. Being able to film Long Day’s Journey Into Night was just a dream come true — although it did start off as a nightmare for a while, because we had no money and were shut down, and it’s been four years getting it to the screen. But stage, screen, TV… as long as the part is there, and you have something to do and it’s thrilling still, then it doesn’t have to be one or the other. It’s any of the above, I think. Don’t you?
paras.zh: 兰格：嗯，我的意思是，这都是这些，取决于角色，取决于公司，取决于很多事情，但我喜欢舞台表演。能够拍摄《漫漫长夜之旅》简直是梦想成真——尽管它一开始确实是一场噩梦，因为我们没有钱，而且被关停了，而且花了四年时间才把它搬上银幕。但是舞台、银幕、电视……只要有这个部分，而且你有事情要做，而且仍然令人兴奋，那么就不必非其中之一。我认为是以上任何一个。你不是吗？

paras.en: PAULSON I agree. I don’t really discriminate, if the part is there, I’ll do it. Wherever someone will have me!
paras.zh: 保尔森 我同意。我并没有真正的歧视，如果有这个部分，我就会做。哪里都会有人有我！

paras.en: SIDIBE When I got the email about AHS: 13, I was actually directing a TV movie. So what came to my mind was: Do I want to be in control of my career? Or step back from the control and go and take a role that I’ve already taken, and somebody else is controlling it? And I did it because I like it, and because in the end, I really don’t have to choose, do I want to be a director or an actor? I’m actually just an artist. I’m going to do my art wherever I am able to do that. And that means acting, it also means directing. It also means producing, because I do want control over the art that I put out into the world.
paras.zh: SIDIBE 当我收到有关《美国恐怖故事：13》的电子邮件时，我实际上正在导演一部电视电影。所以我想到的是：我想掌控自己的职业生涯吗？或者从控制中退一步，去扮演我已经扮演过的角色，而其他人正在控制它？而我这么做是因为我喜欢，而且因为最后我真的不用选择，我是想当导演还是演员？我其实只是一个艺术家。只要我能做到，我就会做我的艺术。这意味着表演，也意味着导演。这也意味着制作，因为我确实想控制我向世界展示的艺术。

paras.en: Having control is really great! We’re all very strong women. Look, a lot of times the lines are there, but we spend a lot of time rewriting these scenes quite a bit. Because we do know these characters. We do know the story, and we are smart. So it’s not that taking a step back as an actor means I have no control. It just means I don’t have top control. But that’s what I want in my career. I want to be able to control the stories that I tell, and I can do this as an actor, but I can do it a little better as a director and a producer. So I have some projects coming up that I’m producing that I’m helping to write, that I’m helping to create. And that’s what I want in my career. I want my own voice.
paras.zh: 有控制力真的很棒！我们都是非常坚强的女性。看，很多时候台词都在那里，但我们花了很多时间重写这些场景。因为我们确实认识这些角色。我们确实知道这个故事，而且我们很聪明。所以作为演员退一步并不意味着我无法控制。这只是意味着我没有最高控制权。但这就是我在职业生涯中想要的。我希望能够控制我所讲述的故事，作为演员我可以做到这一点，但作为导演和制片人我可以做得更好一点。所以我有一些项目正在制作，我正在帮助编写，我正在帮助创建。这就是我在职业生涯中想要的。我想要我自己的声音。

paras.en: LOURD I love it. Everything Gabby said. Control is something that’s also very important to me. I love control. I would say I’m a control freak. (Laughs.) I also am wanting to get into directing and I’ve been producing a lot. I’m also writing a book.
paras.zh: 洛德：我喜欢。盖比所说的一切。控制对我来说也非常重要。我喜欢控制。我想说我是一个控制狂。 （笑）我也想从事导演工作，而且我已经制作了很多作品。我也在写一本书。

paras.en: LANGE How’s that? Is it easy for you to write?
paras.zh: 兰格 怎么样？你写起来容易吗？

paras.en: PAULSON She’s an incredible writer. She shared some of these essays with Leslie and myself when we were shooting.
paras.zh: 保尔森：她是一位令人难以置信的作家。当我们拍摄时，她与莱斯利和我分享了其中一些文章。

paras.en: LOURD It comes very naturally. I love it. It’s my soul thing.
paras.zh: 洛德 这很自然。我喜欢它。这是我灵魂的事。

paras.en: PAULSON She’s also an extraordinary singer. [Quoting Postcards From the Edge, adapted from Lourd’s mother Carrie Fisher’s novel]: “She has a much better voice than that blonde girl. She hasn’t got half your voice.”
paras.zh: 保尔森她也是一位非凡的歌手。 [引用《边缘明信片》，改编自卢德母亲凯莉·费舍尔的小说]：“她的声音比那个金发女孩好得多。她的声音还不到你的一半。”

paras.en: LOURD This woman quoting Postcards is the greatest thing of all time.
paras.zh: 洛德 这位引用明信片的女人是有史以来最伟大的事情。

paras.en: PAULSON I’m quoting her mother’s script. But, really, she’s a woman of many talents. I’d like someone to film it!
paras.zh: 保尔森：我引用的是她母亲的剧本。但事实上，她是一位多才多艺的女性。我想找个人拍一下！

paras.en: New episodes of FX’s American Horror Story: 13 air Thursdays at 9 p.m. on FX and on Hulu, until the finale on Oct. 29.
paras.zh: FX 的《美国恐怖故事》新剧集：每周四晚上 9 点 13 点播出。 FX 和 Hulu 上播出，直至 10 月 29 日大结局。

articles.title: Oasis Documentary ‘Don’t Look Back in Anger’ Hits Streaming: Where to Watch Online
articles.author: Erin Lassner

paras.en: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, The Hollywood Reporter may receive an affiliate commission.
paras.zh: 如果您通过我们网站上的链接购买独立审查的产品或服务，《好莱坞报道》可能会收到附属佣金。

paras.en: Part concert film, part interview-driven doc, Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger provides a backstage (and front-stage) pass to the band’s blockbuster 2025 reunion tour. It also marks the Gallagher brothers’ first joint interview following their 15-year estrangement.
paras.zh: 《绿洲：愤怒中别回头》一半是音乐会影片，一半是采访驱动的纪录片，为乐队 2025 年轰动一时的重聚巡演提供了后台（和前台）通行证。这也标志着加拉格尔兄弟在疏远 15 年后首次接受联合采访。

paras.en: At a Glance: How to Watch Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger
paras.zh: 概览：如何观看《绿洲：不要愤怒地回头》

paras.en: - Stream online: Disney+/Hulu (also included in DirecTV Signature packages’ five-day free trial)
paras.zh: - 在线流媒体：Disney+/Hulu（也包含在 DirecTV Signature 套餐的五天免费试用中）

paras.en: Where to Watch Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger Online: Release Date, Streaming Service
paras.zh: 在哪里观看《绿洲：愤怒中不要回头》在线观看：发行日期、流媒体服务

paras.en: Following its September 2026 theatrical release, Don’t Look Back in Anger makes its streaming debut on Friday, Oct. 9 on Disney+/Hulu, with plans starting at $11.99 per month for the ad-supported package.
paras.zh: 继 2026 年 9 月院线上映后，《愤怒中的别回头》将于 10 月 9 日星期五在 Disney+/Hulu 上首次在线播放，广告支持套餐的起价为每月 11.99 美元。

paras.en: While neither Disney+ nor Hulu offers a trial period directly, fans can get free access through any of DirecTV’s Signature packages, as all four plans (Entertainment, Choice, Ultimate and Premier) include the Disney+ and Hulu bundle and offer a five-day free trial. Following the trial period, DirecTV packages start as low as $20.99 per month.
paras.zh: 虽然 Disney+ 和 Hulu 都没有直接提供试用期，但粉丝可以通过 DirecTV 的任何 Signature 套餐免费访问，因为所有四个计划（娱乐、选择、终极和 Premier）都包含 Disney+ 和 Hulu 捆绑包，并提供五天免费试用。试用期结束后，DirecTV 套餐起价为每月 20.99 美元。

paras.en: Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger Documentary Summary
paras.zh: 绿洲：愤怒中不要回头纪录片摘要

paras.en: Don’t Look Back in Anger is giving viewers unprecedented access to Oasis and the Gallagher brothers. Plus, the streaming release includes bonus content not included in the film’s theatrical version.
paras.zh: 愤怒中不要回头让观众前所未有地了解绿洲和加拉格尔兄弟。此外，流媒体版本还包括电影剧场版中未包含的奖励内容。

paras.en: Per the official synopsis, “Oasis: Don’t Look Back In Anger charts Liam and Noel Gallagher’s triumphant reunion tour, Oasis Live ‘25. Created by Steven Knight, it is an uplifting account of the biggest musical event of 2025, capturing the experience of the band and their fans across the world. It includes rehearsal, backstage, and onstage access as well as the first joint interviews with Noel and Liam in over twenty years.”
paras.zh: 根据官方简介，“《绿洲：不要在愤怒中回头》记录了利亚姆和诺尔·加拉格尔成功重聚巡演 Oasis Live ‘25。由史蒂文·奈特创作，这是对 2025 年最大音乐盛事的令人振奋的描述，捕捉了乐队及其世界各地歌迷的经历。它包括排练、后台和台上参观，以及诺尔和利亚姆二十多年来的首次联合采访年”。

articles.title: New York City man shot in car with child present by ICE agents, mayor says

paras.en: US immigration agents shot and wounded a man on Thursday in his car with a child present in the Marble Hill neighborhood of New York City, according to the mayor, city police and eyewitnesses.
paras.zh: 据市长、市警察和目击者称，周四，美国移民人员在纽约市大理石山社区开枪打伤了一名男子，车上还有一名儿童在场。

paras.en: "Early reports indicate agents surrounded (the man) and a 5-year-old child in his car before firing multiple rounds," New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a statement.
paras.zh: 纽约市长佐兰·马姆达尼 (Zohran Mamdani) 在一份声明中表示：“初步报告显示，特工人员包围了（这名男子）和他车里的一名 5 岁儿童，然后开了多枪。”

paras.en: The mayor said the child was believed to have been physically unharmed.
paras.zh: 市长表示，据信孩子的身体没有受伤。

paras.en: "This is an unconscionable and incredibly serious situation," Mamdani said, adding he planned to speak to President Donald Trump and "demand that he ends all ICE enforcement actions in our city. I will not stand by while ICE agents terrorize our communities."
paras.zh: 马姆达尼说：“这是一个不合理且极其严重的情况。”他补充说，他计划与唐纳德·特朗普总统交谈，并“要求他结束 ICE 在我们城市的所有执法行动。当 ICE 特工恐吓我们的社区时，我不会袖手旁观。”

paras.en: The Department of Homeland Security, ICE's parent agency, said in a statement ICE officers were conducting a "targeted enforcement operation" in the Bronx, New York, to arrest a man from the Dominican Republic with a prior criminal conviction.
paras.zh: ICE 的上级机构国土安全部在一份声明中表示，ICE 官员正在纽约布朗克斯区开展“有针对性的执法行动”，逮捕一名来自多米尼加共和国且有刑事定罪记录的男子。

paras.en: "During the incident, an ICE officer discharged his weapon and the criminal illegal alien was injured," DHS said, adding that ICE officers rendered immediate aid. "The individual is alive and at a local hospital."
paras.zh: 国土安全部表示：“事件中，一名 ICE 官员开枪射击，这名犯罪非法外国人受伤。”并补充说，ICE 官员立即提供了援助。 “此人还活着，在当地一家医院。”

paras.en: The shooting occurred at around 4 p.m. ET (2000 GMT), DHS said.
paras.zh: 枪击事件发生在下午 4 点左右。美国东部时间（格林尼治标准时间 2000 年），国土安全部表示。

paras.en: Working at a restaurant near the shooting, Pedro Almarez said he heard shots fired and went outside to see several officers wearing ICE attire at the scene.
paras.zh: 佩德罗·阿尔马雷斯在枪击事件附近的一家餐厅工作，他说他听到枪声，然后走到外面看到现场有几名穿着 ICE 服装的警察。

paras.en: "There were a lot of ICE officers, three or four cars," Almarez told Reuters by phone, adding the man who was shot appeared to be between 20 and 30 years of age. He said NYPD officers arrived about 10 minutes later. He said the man was only removed from his car after an ambulance arrived.
paras.zh: 阿尔马雷斯通过电话告诉路透社，“现场有很多 ICE 官员，三四辆车。”他补充说，被枪杀的男子年龄在 20 至 30 岁之间。他说纽约警察局官员大约 10 分钟后到达。他说，救护车到达后，这名男子才被从车里抬了出来。

paras.en: At the shooting scene, where police strung yellow crime-scene tape to cordon off a city block, a woman standing on a balcony overlooking the area told officers they were "taking our children," according to a Reuters witness.
paras.zh: 据路透社目击者称，在枪击现场，警方拉起了黄色犯罪现场胶带，封锁了一个街区，一名站在俯瞰该地区的阳台上的妇女告诉警察，他们正在“带走我们的孩子”。

paras.en: Federal immigration agents have shot at least 21 people since Republican President Donald Trump returned to office, 7 fatally, sparking protests across the US. Critics contend that Trump's push to ramp up deportations has led to an increasing number of violent confrontations, and accuse the administration of resisting accountability for the agents involved.
paras.zh: 自共和党总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)重返办公室以来，联邦移民执法人员已枪杀至少21人，其中7人死亡，引发了美国各地的抗议活动。批评者认为，特朗普加大驱逐力度导致暴力冲突数量不断增加，并指责政府拒绝追究相关人员的责任。

articles.title: Ray Dalio warns the stock market's cushion against rising bond yields is shrinking

paras.en: Billionaire investor Ray Dalio warned on Thursday that stocks face mounting pressure from rising bond yields and the prospect of weaker corporate cash flows, even as earnings continue to grow.
paras.zh: 亿万富翁投资者雷·达利奥(Ray Dalio)周四警告称，尽管盈利继续增长，但债券收益率上升和企业现金流疲软前景使股市面临越来越大的压力。

paras.en: The Bridgewater Associates founder told CNBC equities have so far weathered the global bond sell-off because earnings growth has kept expected stock returns attractive, relative to bonds. But that advantage will narrow, he said, potentially leaving equities more vulnerable as financial conditions tighten.
paras.zh: 这位 Bridgewater Associates 创始人告诉 CNBC，迄今为止，股市经受住了全球债券抛售的考验，因为相对于债券而言，盈利增长使预期股票回报率保持有吸引力。但他表示，这种优势将会缩小，随着金融状况收紧，股市可能会更加脆弱。

paras.en: "We're in the part of the cycle where interest rates can rise without sending the equity market down because there's enough earnings growth and there's enough expected return," Dalio told CNBC's Sri Jegarajah at the Milken Institute Asia Summit in Singapore on Thursday.
paras.zh: 达利奥周四在新加坡米尔肯研究所亚洲峰会上对 CNBC 的 Sri Jegarajah 表示：“我们正处于利率上升的周期中，而不会导致股市下跌，因为有足够的盈利增长和足够的预期回报。”

paras.en: "But when that cushion comes down, then you're coming later into that cycle. So that's where we are."
paras.zh: “但是当缓冲下降时，你就会稍后进入这个周期。所以这就是我们现在的处境。”

paras.en: His warning comes as U.S. Treasury yields hover near multi-decade highs. Investors are grappling with large government deficits, persistent inflation and rising borrowing tied to artificial intelligence investment.
paras.zh: 他发出警告之际，美国国债收益率徘徊在数十年高点附近。投资者正在努力应对巨额政府赤字、持续通胀以及与人工智能投资相关的借贷增加。

paras.en: Dalio said equities entered the current cycle offering significantly higher expected returns than bonds, helping sustain demand for stocks even as borrowing costs rose.
paras.zh: 达里奥表示，进入当前周期的股票提供的预期回报明显高于债券，即使借贷成本上升，也有助于维持对股票的需求。

paras.en: But as stock prices climb and bond yields increase, that relative advantage is diminishing, leaving less room for equities to absorb higher rates.
paras.zh: 但随着股价上涨和债券收益率上升，这种相对优势正在减弱，股市吸收更高利率的空间越来越小。

paras.en: "Because of that change in pricing, that cushion has come down, and so now you're starting to see credit spreads start to widen," he said.
paras.zh: “由于定价的变化，缓冲已经下降，所以现在你开始看到信贷利差开始扩大，”他说。

paras.en: Dalio also cautioned that investors may be overlooking the risk of deteriorating corporate cash generation, even as headline earnings continue to improve.
paras.zh: 达利奥还警告说，即使总体盈利持续改善，投资者也可能忽视了企业现金生成能力恶化的风险。

paras.en: Asked whether companies could sustain strong profit growth in the third quarter, Dalio said investors should focus on free cash flow rather than earnings alone.
paras.zh: 当被问及公司第三季度是否能够维持强劲的利润增长时，达里奥表示，投资者应该关注自由现金流，而不仅仅是盈利。

paras.en: "I think you have to pay attention to free cash flows. ... Not just earnings. Because if you're earning and then you're investing and you're not getting money out of that, you have a liquidity issue that's evolving," he said.
paras.zh: “我认为你必须关注自由现金流......不仅仅是收益。因为如果你在赚钱然后进行投资，但你没有从中获得资金，那么你就会面临不断演变的流动性问题，”他说。

paras.en: "While earnings should continue to be improving, I would expect the free cash flows, I think, will be deteriorating."
paras.zh: “虽然盈利应该继续改善，但我认为自由现金流将会恶化。”

paras.en: Dalio stopped short of predicting an earnings decline or an imminent stock market correction. He said financial conditions have not yet tightened enough to significantly curb credit and spending.
paras.zh: 达里奥没有预测盈利下降或股市即将调整。他表示，金融状况尚未收紧到足以大幅抑制信贷和支出的程度。

paras.en: Dalio also said he expected the global bond sell-off to continue as governments and companies compete for capital, as mounting debt issuance puts pressure on investor demand.
paras.zh: 达利奥还表示，他预计全球债券抛售将继续，因为政府和企业争夺资本，不断增加的债务发行给投资者需求带来压力。

paras.en: Governments are borrowing heavily to finance fiscal deficits, while companies are raising funds to invest in emerging technologies, creating an imbalance that could keep upward pressure on interest rates.
paras.zh: 各国政府正在大量举债来弥补财政赤字，而企业则在筹集资金投资新兴技术，从而造成失衡，可能导致利率面临上行压力。

paras.en: "We are in a bond bear market, that's I think, pretty clear, and I think that there's more to go would be my guess," he said.
paras.zh: 他表示：“我认为，我们正处于债券熊市，这一点非常明确，而且我认为还会有更多的事情发生。”

paras.en: Higher borrowing costs will eventually force a reduction in credit and spending, weighing on economic activity and potentially spilling over into equity markets, Dalio said.
paras.zh: 达利奥表示，借贷成本上升最终将迫使信贷和支出减少，从而给经济活动带来压力，并可能波及股市。

paras.en: For now, Dalio said the tightening process is only beginning, with earnings growth still providing support for stocks even as credit conditions start to weaken.
paras.zh: 达里奥表示，目前紧缩进程才刚刚开始，即使信贷状况开始疲软，盈利增长仍为股市提供支撑。

articles.title: Tokenization could unleash tens of billions of dollars in trapped capital, Nasdaq CEO says

paras.en: Tokenization could free up tens of billions of dollars in capital tied up in assets used as collateral across the global financial system, Nasdaq CEO Adena Friedman said.
paras.zh: 纳斯达克首席执行官阿迪娜·弗里德曼 (Adena Friedman) 表示，代币化可以释放全球金融体系中用作抵押品的资产所束缚的数百亿美元资本。

paras.en: Tokenizing assets such as Treasurys, equities and money market funds, along with the flow of money, could make collateral more liquid, Friedman told CNBC's Joanna Ossinger at the TOKEN2049 conference in Singapore.
paras.zh: 弗里德曼在新加坡举行的 TOKEN2049 会议上对 CNBC 的乔安娜·奥辛格 (Joanna Ossinger) 表示，将国债、股票和货币市场基金等资产代币化以及资金流动可以使抵押品更具流动性。

paras.en: "If you tokenize all those instruments along with the flow of money, then the collateral becomes very fluid," Friedman said.
paras.zh: 弗里德曼说：“如果你将所有这些工具与资金流动一起标记化，那么抵押品就会变得非常流动。”

paras.en: Tokenization involves representing financial assets, such as stocks and bonds, as digital tokens that can be transferred using blockchain technology.
paras.zh: 代币化涉及将股票和债券等金融资产表示为可以使用区块链技术转移的数字代币。

paras.en: Friedman said institutional interest in tokenization has grown over the past year, pointing in part to the passage of the Genius Act in the U.S., which established a regulatory framework for stablecoins.
paras.zh: 弗里德曼表示，过去一年机构对代币化的兴趣有所增长，部分原因是美国通过了《天才法案》，该法案为稳定币建立了监管框架。

paras.en: "If we can tokenize money, then we can tokenize the flow of capital," she said.
paras.zh: “如果我们可以将货币代币化，那么我们就可以将资本流动代币化，”她说。

paras.en: That growing institutional interest is converging with demand from retail investors, who have long sought the ability to trade around the clock, according to Friedman. The retail ecosystem "has been about 10 years ahead," she said.
paras.zh: 弗里德曼表示，机构不断增长的兴趣与散户投资者的需求相融合，散户投资者长期以来一直寻求全天候交易的能力。她说，零售生态系统“已经领先了大约十年”。

paras.en: Moving to a fully 24/7 market would be a major undertaking for the financial industry, Friedman said.
paras.zh: 弗里德曼表示，转向完全 24/7 的市场将是金融业的一项重大任务。

paras.en: "The easiest part is the exchange infrastructure," she said.
paras.zh: “最简单的部分是交换基础设施，”她说。

paras.en: Friedman said that financial institutions have traditionally had periods when markets are closed to update systems and manage risk. But operating around the clock would require those processes, including risk and collateral management, to take place continuously.
paras.zh: 弗里德曼表示，金融机构传统上都会有市场休市的时期，以更新系统和管理风险。但全天候运营需要这些流程（包括风险和抵押品管理）持续进行。

paras.en: "Everything has to be real time all the time," she said.
paras.zh: “一切都必须始终是实时的，”她说。

paras.en: Artificial intelligence could help financial institutions manage that transition. Nasdaq has launched a series of digital agents within its risk management platform that initially provide recommendations, Friedman said.
paras.zh: 人工智能可以帮助金融机构管理这种转变。弗里德曼表示，纳斯达克在其风险管理平台内推出了一系列数字代理，最初提供建议。

paras.en: Over time, banks could use those agents to take more direct action, she added.
paras.zh: 她补充说，随着时间的推移，银行可以利用这些代理人采取更直接的行动。

paras.en: "AI is critical for 24/7," Friedman said.
paras.zh: “人工智能对于 24/7 至关重要，”弗里德曼说。

paras.en: Companies outside the U.S. are showing interest in tokenization and access to American capital markets, Arjun Sethi, co-CEO of cryptocurrency exchange Kraken, told CNBC.
paras.zh: 加密货币交易所 Kraken 联合首席执行官 Arjun Sethi 告诉 CNBC，美国以外的公司对代币化和进入美国资本市场表现出了兴趣。

paras.en: Sethi pointed to a company generating roughly $25 million in revenue that was exploring ways to access capital markets, as well as larger international companies interested in tokenization and U.S. public listings.
paras.zh: Sethi 指出，一家年收入约 2500 万美元的公司正在探索进入资本市场的方式，还有一些对代币化和美国公开上市感兴趣的大型国际公司。

paras.en: He said tokenization could help expand access to capital markets for companies around the world.
paras.zh: 他表示，代币化可以帮助世界各地的公司扩大进入资本市场的机会。

paras.en: However, round-the-clock trading may not be suitable for everything, according to Friedman.
paras.zh: 然而，弗里德曼表示，全天候交易可能并不适合所有情况。

paras.en: "Not every asset is liquid enough to support a 24/7 environment," she said.
paras.zh: “并非所有资产的流动性都足以支持 24/7 环境，”她说。

paras.en: Still, greater connectivity across the global financial system could also open up access to asset classes that were previously out of reach for some investors, Friedman said.
paras.zh: 弗里德曼表示，尽管如此，全球金融体系的互联互通也可能为一些投资者提供以前无法接触到的资产类别。

articles.title: Astronomers discover record-breaking ancient cosmic outburst

paras.en: At some point around three billion years after the big bang, some celestial object in a faraway galaxy suddenly went pop and shot out a brief-but-powerful blast of radio waves, lasting just a fraction of a second. That blast kept traveling across the intergalactic vastness of space and time until, in March 2024, it breezed by Earth, with a small fraction of its energy trickling into the dishes of the MeerKAT radio telescope array in South Africa.
paras.zh: 在大爆炸后大约三十亿年的某个时刻，遥远星系中的某个天体突然爆炸，发射出短暂但强大的无线电波爆炸，持续时间只有几分之一秒。那股爆炸继续穿越银河系浩瀚的时空，直到 2024 年 3 月，它微风掠过地球，其中一小部分能量流入南非 MeerKAT 射电望远镜阵列的碟形天线中。

paras.en: For Themiya Nanayakkara, an astronomer at Australia’s University of Sydney, MeerKAT’s detection was a moment of peak excitement. Fast radio bursts (FRBs), as these types of emissions are called, are common, occurring roughly 5,000 to 10,000 times per day across Earth’s sky. But this one’s sheer faintness signaled it was very old, originating long, long ago from somewhere far, far away.
paras.zh: 对于澳大利亚悉尼大学天文学家 Themiya Nanayakkara 来说，MeerKAT 的发现是一个最兴奋的时刻。这些类型的发射被称为快速无线电爆发 (FRB)，这种现象很常见，每天在地球天空中发生大约 5,000 到 10,000 次。但这颗的光芒完全暗淡，表明它非常古老，来自很久很久以前，来自很远很远的地方。

paras.en: But just how old was it, and where did it come from? Looking at the power of the burst and the amount of its light that had been stretched, or “redshifted,” by the expansion of the universe around it as it traveled, Nanayakkara and his colleagues were able to find out. As they describe in a new paper in Science, this FRB occurred in a far-distant galaxy some 10 billion years ago. That esteemed cosmic vintage makes this the oldest FRB ever detected by far. This event, in fact, is twice as old as the previous record holder.
paras.zh: 但它到底有多大年纪，又是从哪里来的呢？纳纳亚卡拉和他的同事们观察了爆发的力量，以及在其传播过程中由于周围宇宙的膨胀而被拉伸或“红移”的光量，纳纳亚卡拉和他的同事们能够找到答案。正如他们在《科学》杂志上发表的一篇新论文中所描述的那样，这种快速射电暴发生在大约 100 亿年前的一个遥远星系中。这种受人尊敬的宇宙年份使其成为迄今为止探测到的最古老的快速射电暴。事实上，这一赛事的历史是之前的纪录保持者的两倍。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Despite intensive scrutiny in the quarter-century since their discovery, FRBs remain rather mysterious. For starters, astronomers still don’t know their astrophysical origins. One leading idea posits they’re produced by magnetars, small remnants left behind by massive stars that detonate as supernovae, but many details are murky, and not all FRBs seem to fit the “magnetar” mold. Detecting and measuring FRBs and their host galaxies can help solve the puzzle, Nanayakkara says. In this case, he and his colleagues traced this one back to a galaxy that appears relatively primitive compared with others from its early cosmic epoch: this galaxy has a lower mass and less heavy elements than its contemporaries but higher amounts of star formation.
paras.zh: 尽管自发现以来的四分之一个世纪里人们对快速射电暴进行了深入的研究，但快速射电暴仍然相当神秘。首先，天文学家仍然不知道它们的天体物理起源。一个主要观点认为它们是由磁星产生的，磁星是大质量恒星爆炸为超新星时留下的小残余物，但许多细节尚不清楚，而且并非所有快速射电暴似乎都符合“磁星”模式。纳纳亚卡拉说，探测和测量快速射电暴及其宿主星系可以帮助解决这个难题。在这种情况下，他和他的同事们将这个星系追溯到一个与早期宇宙时代的其他星系相比显得相对原始的星系：这个星系比同时代的星系具有更低的质量和更少的重元素，但恒星形成的数量更高。

paras.en: None of that is necessarily unexpected for the formation of an FRB-birthing magnetar. But this record-setting FRB still significantly pushes back the baseline for when these bursts can occur in cosmic history. And according to Nanayakkara, this in turn raises the possibility that even older (and fainter) FRBs have passed by Earth unnoticed.
paras.zh: 对于 FRB 诞生磁星的形成来说，这一切都不一定是意外的。但这一创纪录的快速射电暴仍然大大推后了宇宙历史上这些爆发何时发生的基线。根据 Nanayakkara 的说法，这反过来又增加了一种可能性，即更古老（更微弱）的快速射电暴在不被注意的情况下掠过地球。

paras.en: “Our telescopes need to be extremely sensitive to detect them,” he says. Thankfully, MeerKAT exists to help. “The same thing applies when trying to find their host galaxies. Since these galaxies are also very far away, they can be extremely faint, making it challenging to follow them up and study their properties.”
paras.zh: “我们的望远镜需要极其灵敏才能探测到它们，”他说。值得庆幸的是，MeerKAT 的存在是为了提供帮助。 “当试图寻找它们的宿主星系时，同样的情况也适用。由于这些星系也非常遥远，它们可能非常微弱，这使得跟踪它们并研究它们的特性变得具有挑战性。”

paras.en: The clamor to find and study increasingly distant FRBs isn’t just a matter of curiosity, either: These short, sharp bursts can also serve as potent probes of otherwise-invisible matter spread between galaxies. As an FRB travels, its radio waves interact with the dilute, dark plasma that astronomers call the intergalactic medium; the FRB’s shorter waves interact more with the plasma, slowing their propagation so that they arrive at Earth later than their longer-wavelength counterparts. Measuring this dispersion allows astronomers to learn just how much of this material any given FRB has traversed on its long journey to our planet.
paras.zh: 寻找和研究距离越来越远的快速射电暴的呼声也不仅仅是出于好奇：这些短暂而尖锐的爆发也可以作为对星系之间传播的不可见物质的有效探测器。当快速射电暴传播时，它的无线电波与天文学家称之为星系际介质的稀暗暗等离子体相互作用。 FRB 的较短波与等离子体的相互作用更多，减慢了它们的传播速度，因此它们比较长波长的波更晚到达地球。通过测量这种色散，天文学家可以了解任何给定的快速射电暴在到达地球的漫长旅程中经过了多少这种物质。

paras.en: “Our discovery is particularly important because we have shown that we can do this across approximately 80 percent of cosmic history,” Nanayakkara says. “The further back we push FRB detections, the further we can map this otherwise unseen matter.”
paras.zh: “我们的发现特别重要，因为我们已经证明我们可以在大约 80% 的宇宙历史中做到这一点，”Nanayakkara 说。 “我们将 FRB 探测推得越远，我们就越能绘制出这种看不见的物质的图谱。”

paras.en: To accomplish this, Nanayakkara recently secured time on NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). Once a year for the next three years, his team will be able to focus JWST onto the faraway astrophysical source of some especially ancient FRB, seeking to break the cosmic distance record yet again.
paras.zh: 为了实现这一目标，Nanayakkara 最近在 NASA 的詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜 (JWST) 上获得了时间。在接下来的三年里，他的团队每年将能够将 JWST 聚焦到一些特别古老的 FRB 的遥远天体物理源上，寻求再次打破宇宙距离记录。

paras.en: “We are currently waiting for our radio telescopes in Australia and South Africa to detect such a burst. As soon as we find one, we can trigger JWST observations to study its host galaxy and hopefully push the boundary even further,” he says. “The more distant FRBs we find, the stronger the constraints we can place on the objects and emission mechanisms that produce them, the environments in which they occur and the distribution of matter across the universe.”
paras.zh: “我们目前正在等待澳大利亚和南非的射电望远镜探测到这样的爆发。一旦发现，我们就可以触发 JWST 观测来研究其宿主星系，并有望进一步推动边界，”他说。 “我们发现的快速射电暴距离越远，我们对产生它们的物体和发射机制、它们发生的环境以及物质在宇宙中的分布的限制就越强。”

articles.title: Mathematicians marvel, and grumble, at OpenAI’s trove of new results

paras.en: It’s been two days since OpenAI’s “slop drop” of AI-generated results on 372 open math and computer science problems. Scientists are just beginning to parse through the heap and pick out the most exciting breakthroughs in their own fields.
paras.zh: 距离 OpenAI “倾斜”发布 372 个开放数学和计算机科学问题的 AI 生成结果已经过去两天了。科学家们刚刚开始解析这些堆数据，并挑选出自己领域中最令人兴奋的突破。

paras.en: It will be months, perhaps years, before we understand just how much novel mathematics was added to the literature this week, but everyone agrees it’s been a week without precedent. “Yesterday will be the day when a new era of math and mathematical physics began,” Harvard University mathematician Michael Douglas told Scientific American on Tuesday. It was an even bigger moment, he thinks, than last month’s solution of the Navier-Stokes problem, one of math’s million-dollar challenges, by the same new internal model at OpenAI.
paras.zh: 我们需要几个月甚至几年的时间才能了解本周文献中添加了多少新颖的数学，但每个人都同意这是史无前例的一周。 “昨天将是数学和数学物理新时代开始的一天，”哈佛大学数学家迈克尔·道格拉斯周二告诉《科学美国人》。他认为，这比上个月 OpenAI 相同的新内部模型解决纳维-斯托克斯问题（数学百万美元挑战之一）的解决方案更重要。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Already certain aspects of this new era are becoming clear. Many of the results, experts say, are far better written than the Navier-Stokes proof, suggesting that OpenAI’s math team is working to overcome its model’s inability to explain its math clearly to humans. Hector Pasten, a mathematician at the Pontifical Catholic University of Chile, says the papers he’s looked at improve on the company’s notorious lack of citations. “I think they are doing a better job of giving credit,” he says.
paras.zh: 这个新时代的某些方面已经变得清晰起来。专家表示，许多结果比纳维-斯托克斯证明要好得多，这表明 OpenAI 的数学团队正在努力克服其模型无法向人类清楚解释数学的问题。智利天主教大学数学家赫克托·帕斯滕 (Hector Pasten) 表示，他所研究的论文改善了该公司臭名昭著的缺乏引用的问题。 “我认为他们在给予信任方面做得更好，”他说。

paras.en: But the quality remains extremely uneven—mathematicians are finding some papers readable and others utterly nonsensical. “Others are much, much harder to make sense of—they’re sort of this AI slop,” says Roland Bauerschmidt, a mathematician at New York University. “If I had received these by e-mail from a nobody, I probably would have deleted it, it’s so badly written.”
paras.zh: 但质量仍然极其参差不齐——数学家发现一些论文可读，而另一些则完全毫无意义。纽约大学数学家罗兰·鲍尔施密特 (Roland Bauerschmidt) 表示：“其他的则很难理解——它们有点像人工智能的废话。” “如果我通过电子邮件收到这些，我可能会删除它，它写得太糟糕了。”

paras.en: Even much of that seeming nonsense, though, is ostensibly correct. At this point, 42 percent of the results are coded in the programming language Lean, which means their logic is almost certainly sound, even if their English-language write-up is too hard to follow.
paras.zh: 不过，即使很多看似无稽之谈，表面上也是正确的。此时，42% 的结果是用 Lean 编程语言编码的，这意味着它们的逻辑几乎肯定是正确的，即使它们的英文书写太难以理解。

paras.en: On the other hand, three of the papers have already been withdrawn after experts uncovered a significant error, causing some to question the more than half of the proofs that aren’t yet Lean-verified. “While I expect most of these will ultimately be found to be correct, or at least correctable, we should expect some of the proofs to contain mistakes, possibly serious ones,” says Andrew Sutherland, a mathematician at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
paras.zh: 另一方面，在专家发现一个重大错误后，其中三篇论文已经被撤回，导致一些人对一半以上尚未经过精益验证的证明提出质疑。麻省理工学院数学家安德鲁·萨瑟兰（Andrew Sutherland）表示：“虽然我预计其中大部分最终都会被证明是正确的，或者至少是可以纠正的，但我们应该预料到一些证明会包含错误，甚至可能是严重的错误。”

paras.en: The community’s reaction to the way OpenAI chose to drop the results has been mixed, to say the least. Sutherland argues that OpenAI should also release the problems its model failed to solve, which the company has said number in the thousands. “I expect they will not want to do that,” he adds, “but that is how open science works. You need to report your negative results along with your positive results.”
paras.zh: 至少可以说，社区对 OpenAI 选择放弃结果的方式反应不一。 Sutherland 认为 OpenAI 还应该公布其模型未能解决的问题，该公司称此类问题有数千个。 “我预计他们不会愿意这样做，”他补充道，“但这就是开放科学的运作方式。你需要在报告积极结果的同时报告你的消极结果。”

paras.en: The lack of transparency goes further. A number of mathematicians have told Scientific American that they doubt anyone on OpenAI’s team would have thought to ask some of the questions the model answered, either because they’re extremely niche or because they contradict a belief most experts previously held. Several independently suggested that it seems the model itself is coming up with problems to solve, perhaps in an extended conversation between a swarm of agents. This idea seems corroborated by the fact that a number of papers contain strikingly similar ideas and methods—as if their authors were communicating. OpenAI didn’t reply to a request for comment on this question.
paras.zh: 缺乏透明度的情况更进一步。许多数学家告诉《科学美国人》，他们怀疑 OpenAI 团队中的任何人都会考虑提出该模型所回答的一些问题，要么是因为这些问题非常小众，要么是因为它们与大多数专家之前持有的信念相矛盾。一些人独立地表示，模型本身似乎正在提出需要解决的问题，也许是在一群智能体之间的长时间对话中。许多论文包含惊人相似的想法和方法，这一事实似乎证实了这一观点——就好像它们的作者在交流一样。 OpenAI 没有回复对此问题的置评请求。

paras.en: Others in the community have been more outspoken in their criticism. A statement from the Association for Human Mathematics decries the company’s actions. “Releasing over 700 files at once is not a demonstration of scholarship, but a demonstration of power,” it reads. “We urge mathematicians to discontinue their work with OpenAI and to return to a vision of science that centers human understanding.”
paras.zh: 社区中的其他人则更加直言不讳地提出批评。人类数学协会的一份声明谴责了该公司的行为。 “一次性公布700多个文件不是学术的展示，而是权力的展示，”它写道。 “我们敦促数学家停止与 OpenAI 的合作，回归以人类理解为中心的科学愿景。”

articles.title: The most exciting claims from OpenAI’s heap of new proofs

paras.en: On Tuesday afternoon OpenAI dropped more than 700 manuscripts reporting proofs, solutions and progress on 372 open problems across theoretical research.
paras.zh: 周二下午，OpenAI 发布了 700 多份手稿，报告了理论研究中 372 个开放问题的证明、解决方案和进展。

paras.en: It will take time for mathematicians to trudge through all the artificial-intelligence-generated results. No one, not even OpenAI researchers themselves, has been able to even read through everything yet. And not all of the proofs were certified as correct by the automatic logic verification platform Lean—in fact, some have already been retracted after outside scientists found mistakes. OpenAI also did not include full prompts or run-time details for how their agents uncovered the proofs, and officials admitted in a blog post about the results that citations and written descriptions of findings could be improved in future releases.
paras.zh: 数学家需要时间来研究所有人工智能生成的结果。目前还没有人能够读懂所有内容，甚至包括 OpenAI 研究人员本身。并不是所有的证明都被自动逻辑验证平台 Lean 证明是正确的——事实上，有些证据在外部科学家发现错误后已经被撤回。 OpenAI 也没有提供有关其代理如何发现证据的完整提示或运行时详细信息，官员们在一篇有关结果的博客文章中承认，在未来的版本中可以改进对结果的引用和书面描述。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Despite these issues, experts say the results are jaw-dropping. The papers span mathematics, theoretical computer science, physics, and more. Some of the discoveries could have easily netted a human author a top research award just a year ago
paras.zh: 尽管存在这些问题，专家表示结果还是令人瞠目结舌。这些论文涵盖数学、理论计算机科学、物理学等。就在一年前，其中一些发现可以轻松地为人类作者赢得最高研究奖

paras.en: Here are just some of the most important problems OpenAI claims to have solved, according to the experts.
paras.zh: 专家们表示，以下只是 OpenAI 声称已经解决的一些最重要的问题。

paras.en: The Riemann hypothesis is the scariest open problem in math—experts told Scientific American earlier this year that they barely think about it because they have no idea how to even start tackling it. That might have just changed.
paras.zh: 黎曼猜想是数学中最可怕的开放性问题——专家们今年早些时候告诉《科学美国人》，他们几乎没有考虑过这个问题，因为他们甚至不知道如何开始解决它。这可能刚刚改变。

paras.en: The hypothesis centers on a special, complicated equation called the Riemann zeta function—specifically, which numbers you can put into this function to make it come out to zero. If you could magically know all of these special inputs, you would essentially know all of the prime numbers—mathematicians’ favorite objects and the building blocks of the entire number line.
paras.zh: 该假设以一个称为黎曼 zeta 函数的特殊复杂方程为中心，具体来说，您可以将哪些数字放入该函数中以使其结果为零。如果你能神奇地知道所有这些特殊输入，你基本上就会知道所有素数——数学家最喜欢的物体和整个数轴的构建块。

paras.en: OpenAI’s drop contains two major results about these “zeros.” One proves the “quasi-Riemann hypothesis,” which is a huge step toward the holy grail of proving the full thing. “Plenty of applications of the Riemann hypothesis did not need the full Riemann hypothesis,” says Hector Pasten, a mathematician at the Pontifical Catholic University of Chile. “The quasi-Riemann hypothesis is way more than enough for many applications.” For instance, mathematicians now have a better estimate of where the primes sit as you go up the number line than they ever had before.
paras.zh: OpenAI 的下降包含有关这些“零”的两个主要结果。有人证明了“准黎曼假设”，这是朝着证明全部事实的圣杯迈出的一大步。 “黎曼假设的大量应用并不需要完整的黎曼假设，”智利天主教大学数学家赫克托·帕斯滕 (Hector Pasten) 说。 “拟黎曼假设对于许多应用来说已经足够了。”例如，数学家现在可以比以前更好地估计沿着数轴上升时素数的位置。

paras.en: As to whether this proof is a path toward solving the full hypothesis, it’s too early to say. “Some people claim it is progress toward Riemann; other people say it’s not,” Pasten says. “Usually the word progress makes sense after the fact, when you see how it eventually gets solved.”
paras.zh: 至于这个证明是否是解决整个假设的一条途径，现在说还为时过早。 “有些人声称这是向黎曼迈进；其他人则说不是，”帕斯滕说。 “通常，当你看到问题最终如何得到解决时，“进步”这个词才有意义。”

paras.en: The second result shows that neither the zeta function nor many of its generalizations, called “Dirichlet L-functions,” have a “Siegel zero,” a certain, especially problematic type of zero that would contradict the hypothesis. “This is not just progress on Siegel zeros—it settles the question,” Pasten says. “This is amazing.”
paras.zh: 第二个结果表明，zeta 函数及其许多推广（称为“狄利克雷 L 函数”）都没有“西格尔零”，这是一种与假设相矛盾的特定的、特别有问题的零类型。 “这不仅仅是西格尔零点的进展——它解决了问题，”帕斯滕说。 “这太棒了。”

paras.en: Hilbert’s 10th problem is about which mathematical truths are and are not knowable. It asks whether it’s possible to build an algorithm that sorts all simple algebra problems into two piles. One pile holds equations that have whole-number solutions, such as y2 = 2x (where x = 2 and y = 2 is a solution). The other pile consists of equations without a solution in which the variables are whole numbers, such as y2 + x2 = –1.
paras.zh: 希尔伯特的第十个问题是关于哪些数学真理是可知的，哪些是不可知的。它询问是否可以构建一种算法，将所有简单的代数问题分为两堆。一堆包含具有整数解的方程，例如 y2 = 2x（其中 x = 2 和 y = 2 是一个解）。另一堆由没有解的方程组成，其中变量是整数，例如 y2 + x2 = –1。

paras.en: In 1970 mathematician Yuri Matiyasevich showed that such an algorithm is impossible. No computer can tell you whether or not any equation has a solution with whole numbers. But since then mathematicians have been struggling to extend this result, asking if a computer can sort equations when you allow their variables to have a wider range of values, such as fractions, square roots or imaginary numbers. OpenAI’s model proved that even when the variables are allowed to be any rational number—a whole number or a fraction—the mathematical world remains unsortable.
paras.zh: 1970 年，数学家 Yuri Matiyasevich 证明这样的算法是不可能的。没有计算机可以告诉你任何方程是否有整数解。但从那时起，数学家们一直在努力扩展这个结果，询问当你允许方程的变量具有更广泛的值（例如分数、平方根或虚数）时，计算机是否可以对方程进行排序。 OpenAI 的模型证明，即使变量可以是任何有理数（整数或分数），数学世界仍然是不可排序的。

paras.en: The new proof uses two of Pasten’s ideas from seemingly different areas of mathematics—even he hadn’t realized they could be put together in this way. “It’s extremely surprising to me that they connect,” Pasten says. “Their general strategy is original.”
paras.zh: 新的证明使用了帕斯滕的两个看似不同的数学领域的想法——即使他也没有意识到它们可以以这种方式组合在一起。 “他们之间的联系让我感到非常惊讶，”帕斯滕说。 “他们的总体策略是原创的。”

paras.en: The Kakeya conjecture can be thought of as sliding and twirling a piece of chalk around on a tablet so that it points in every direction but covers as small an area with chalk as possible. Mathematician Hong Wang won a Fields medal this summer for solving the three-dimensional version of this problem with mathematician Joshua Zahl. In that version, you twirl the stick around in midair—showing the minimum possible 3D space the twirl can occupy. Now OpenAI’s model has solved the problem for four dimensions.
paras.zh: 挂谷猜想可以被认为是在平板电脑上滑动和旋转一块粉笔，使其指向各个方向，但用粉笔覆盖尽可能小的区域。今年夏天，数学家王宏因与数学家约书亚·扎尔 (Joshua Zahl) 一起解决了该问题的三维版本而获得了菲尔兹奖。在该版本中，您在半空中旋转棍子 - 显示旋转可以占据的最小可能的 3D 空间。现在OpenAI的模型已经从四个维度解决了这个问题。

paras.en: Other important number theory results include Artin’s conjecture on primitive roots, which is about special number systems that stop at a certain, highest number, as well as a proof of perhaps the most famous conjecture of storied problem-poser Paul Erdős and progress that is relevant to the Langlands program, a sweeping set of conjectures sometimes called “a Grand Unified Theory of Mathematics.”
paras.zh: 其他重要的数论成果包括阿廷关于原根的猜想，该猜想涉及到停止于某个最高数字的特殊数系，以及对著名问题提出者保罗·埃尔多斯（Paul Erdős）最著名的猜想的证明，以及与朗兰兹纲领相关的进展，朗兰兹纲领是一组广泛的猜想，有时被称为“数学大统一理论”。

paras.en: On its face, the “nonlinear sigma model” doesn’t sound like it has anything to do with particle physics. At every point on a grid, you place an arrow in a different direction to represent interacting, spinning atoms. The goal is to show that rotations of the arrows in one place cannot be detected far away. But that aim bears a striking, hidden resemblance to “the Yang-Mills existence and mass gap problem,” one of the five remaining Millennium Prize Problems, which aims to underpin the “Standard Model” of particle physics with rigorous mathematics. “This goes back 50 years, much like Yang-Mills, and is widely considered the ‘warm-up’ for Yang-Mills,” says Michael Douglas, a mathematical physicist at Harvard University.
paras.zh: 从表面上看，“非线性西格玛模型”听起来与粒子物理学没有任何关系。在网格上的每个点上，您都可以在不同方向上放置一个箭头来表示相互作用、旋转的原子。目标是证明箭头在一个地方的旋转无法在很远的地方被检测到。但这一目标与“杨-米尔斯存在性和质量间隙问题”有着惊人的、隐藏的相似之处，这是剩下的五个千年奖问题之一，旨在用严格的数学来支撑粒子物理学的“标准模型”。哈佛大学数学物理学家迈克尔·道格拉斯 (Michael Douglas) 表示：“这可以追溯到 50 年前，就像杨米尔斯一样，并且被广泛认为是杨米尔斯的‘热身’。”

paras.en: OpenAI’s repository contains several papers claiming to completely resolve the equivalent of the Yang-Mills problem for this simpler model. New York University mathematician Roland Bauerschmidt says the first of these papers is both groundbreaking and comprehensible. “I haven’t digested it or understood all the details, but it seems very reasonable,” he says. The rest of the papers related to this problem are incomprehensible slop, he says, too hard for even a human expert to verify. “The second paper is horrible,” Bauerschmidt says. “If these results had been sent to me by a nobody, I would have deleted the e-mail.”
paras.zh: OpenAI 的存储库包含几篇论文，声称完全解决了这个更简单模型的 Yang-Mills 问题的等效问题。纽约大学数学家罗兰·鲍尔施密特表示，第一篇论文既具有开创性又易于理解。 “我还没有消化它或理解所有细节，但它看起来非常合理，”他说。他说，与这个问题相关的其余论文都是难以理解的废话，即使是人类专家也很难验证。 “第二篇论文太糟糕了，”鲍尔施密特说。 “如果这些结果是由任何人发送给我的，我就会删除该电子邮件。”

paras.en: Physicists know a strange state of matter called the “Bose-Einstein condensate” is possible because researchers have made it in a lab—winning them the 2001 Nobel Prize in Physics. This material is where all the atoms in a gas occupy the exact same quantum state, producing weird quantum effects at unusually macroscopic scales. Albert Einstein originally predicted its existence in work that built upon a 1924 paper by physicist Satyendra Nath Bose, but he only proved that the state is mathematically possible for an unrealistic gas where no two atoms interact. OpenAI’s model extended the prediction to a case with interactions. It used similar techniques to prove a major conjecture about the math of ferromagnetism—one that the famous mathematical physicist Freeman Dyson erroneously claimed with two collaborators in 1976.
paras.zh: 物理学家知道一种被称为“玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚”的奇怪物质状态是可能存在的，因为研究人员已经在实验室中实现了这种状态，并为他们赢得了 2001 年诺贝尔物理学奖。在这种材料中，气体中的所有原子都占据完全相同的量子态，在异常宏观尺度上产生奇怪的量子效应。阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦最初在物理学家 Satyendra Nath Bose 1924 年发表的论文基础上预测了这种状态的存在，但他只是证明了对于没有两个原子相互作用的不切实际的气体来说，这种状态在数学上是可能的。 OpenAI 的模型将预测扩展到具有交互的案例。它使用类似的技术来证明一个关于铁磁性数学的重大猜想——著名数学物理学家弗里曼·戴森 (Freeman Dyson) 与两名合作者在 1976 年错误地提出了这个猜想。

paras.en: Anyone who's taken a linear algebra course can attest that matrices—ensembles of numbers in a two-dimensional array—underpin many different fields of computer science. Manipulating and performing operations on them quickly is important for computer graphics, complex simulations and machine learning itself. “Matrix multiplication is needed all over the place," says Virginia Vassilevska Williams, a computer science professor at MIT who researches the problem. "But also, its complexity is one of the great mysteries in computer science." Multiplying two matrices together requires a tedious amount of arithmetic.
paras.zh: 任何学习过线性代数课程的人都可以证明矩阵（二维数组中的数字集合）是计算机科学许多不同领域的基础。快速操纵和执行它们对于计算机图形、复杂模拟和机器学习本身非常重要。 “到处都需要矩阵乘法，”研究这个问题的麻省理工学院计算机科学教授 Virginia Vassilevska Williams 说。 “而且，它的复杂性也是计算机科学中最大的谜团之一。”将两个矩阵相乘需要大量繁琐的算术。

paras.en: The number of mathematical operations it takes to do these matrix multiplications scales with the cube of the length of the matrices. Scientists have sought a way to shrink the size of the exponent. If they had to do fewer than a cube of the length, it could mean exponential time savings. A few years ago, Vassilevska Williams and her colleagues had gotten that exponent down from 3 to around 2.37, the lowest ever achieved. Problem 107 claims a new lowest boundof 9⁄4, or 2.25. Paper 109 supposedly uses similar methods to find new, faster ways to multiply integers together, too. “In a maybe diabolical sense, the advance on matrix multiplication can be seen as an attempt by the LLMs to speed themselves up," Vassilevska Williams says.
paras.zh: 进行这些矩阵乘法所需的数学运算数量与矩阵长度的立方成正比。科学家们正在寻找一种缩小指数大小的方法。如果他们必须做的长度少于立方体，则可能意味着指数级的时间节省。几年前，Vassilevska Williams 和她的同事将该指数从 3 降至 2.37 左右，这是有史以来达到的最低值。问题 107 声称新的最低界限为 9⁄4，即 2.25。 Paper 109 据说也使用类似的方法来寻找新的、更快的整数相乘方法。 “从某种意义上来说，矩阵乘法的进步可以被视为法学硕士为加快自己的速度而做出的尝试，”Vassilevska Williams 说。

paras.en: If algorithms research is about the best ways to solve problems, complexity theory asks the reverse: How hard is it to find the best solutions to problems—the ideal algorithms that can’t be beat? This challenge involves thinking about what kinds of resources a computer has at its disposal and asking which resources let one solve more problems. A classic quandary about problems computers can solve called P versus NP, likely one of the hardest of the Millenium Prize Problems, is perhaps the most famous complexity problem.
paras.zh: 如果算法研究是关于解决问题的最佳方法，那么复杂性理论则提出了相反的问题：找到问题的最佳解决方案（不可击败的理想算法）有多难？这一挑战涉及思考计算机可以使用哪些类型的资源，并询问哪些资源可以让人们解决更多问题。关于计算机可以解决的问题的经典难题称为 P 与 NP，这可能是千年奖问题中最难的问题之一，也可能是最著名的复杂性问题。

paras.en: A key to both algorithms and complexity is asking how the solution or problem scales with the size of its input. For example, in the case of multiplication, researchers would want to know not just the best way to multiply two 100-digit numbers but how long it takes to multiply numbers of any size as a function of how many digits they have.
paras.zh: 算法和复杂性的关键是询问解决方案或问题如何随着输入的大小而扩展。例如，在乘法的情况下，研究人员不仅想知道两个 100 位数字相乘的最佳方法，还想知道将任意大小的数字相乘需要多长时间，作为数字位数的函数。

paras.en: L, also known as LOGSPACE, is the complexity class of problems that can be answered with very little space—logarithmic in the size of the problem’s description. RL and BPL, meanwhile, are randomized versions of LOGSPACE in which the computer can harness randomness and only needs to be right most of the time. Proving that L = RL = BPL, as Problem 103 claims to do, shows that every problem of this type that can be done with randomness can also be done without it, known as derandomization.
paras.zh: L，也称为 LOGSPACE，是可以用非常小的空间（问题描述的大小的对数）来回答的问题的复杂性类别。与此同时，RL 和 BPL 是 LOGSPACE 的随机版本，其中计算机可以利用随机性，并且只需要在大多数时间都是正确的。正如问题 103 声称的那样，证明 L = RL = BPL 表明，可以使用随机性完成的此类问题也可以在没有随机性的情况下完成，称为去随机化。

paras.en: In practice, computer programs use randomness all the time, but many researchers think it probably doesn’t speed up algorithms. “We have strong reasons to believe that, but we don’t know how to prove it,” says Ran Raz, a complexity theorist at Princeton University. While there was evidence that L = RL was likely to be true, proving it directly has been elusive until now. “I didn’t see any directions that were promising [before],” Raz says.
paras.zh: 在实践中，计算机程序一直在使用随机性，但许多研究人员认为它可能不会加快算法速度。 “我们有充分的理由相信这一点，但我们不知道如何证明这一点，”普林斯顿大学复杂性理论家兰·拉兹说。虽然有证据表明 L = RL 可能是正确的，但迄今为止直接证明这一点还很难。 “（之前）我没有看到任何有希望的方向，”拉兹说。

paras.en: The unique games conjecture also falls under complexity theory. First pitched in 2002, it implicitly asks how hard it is, given a set of constraints, to satisfy some portion of them. Here the resource under the microscope is approximation—that is, instead of getting an exactly correct answer to a given problem, the computer only needs to get close to the answer. Although the unique games problem isn’t explicitly about approximation, showing that it’s difficult would imply that finding approximate answers to many problems is as hard as finding the answer directly.
paras.zh: 独特博弈猜想也属于复杂性理论的范畴。它于 2002 年首次提出，含蓄地询问了在给定一组约束的情况下满足其中某些约束有多难。这里显微镜下的资源是近似值——也就是说，计算机不需要得到给定问题的完全正确的答案，而只需接近答案即可。尽管独特的游戏问题没有明确地涉及近似，但表明它很困难意味着找到许多问题的近似答案与直接找到答案一样困难。

paras.en: Problem 102 claims to do just that, proving that the unique games problem is hard. This solution has been a bit controversial. Other researchers who had caught wind of OpenAI’s work on the problem rushed out their partial progress toward the answer in fear of being scooped by AI.
paras.zh: 问题 102 声称可以做到这一点，证明独特的博弈问题是困难的。这个解决方案引起了一些争议。其他听说了 OpenAI 在这个问题上的研究成果的研究人员担心被 AI 抢先，因此急忙拿出部分进展来寻找答案。

paras.en: Over in the land of quantum computing, meanwhile, Problem 283 could give a better picture at how difficult truly quantum problems are. Scientists understand how bits in a classical computer work and can be manipulated, but they have less of a handle on quantum computing’s analogue to the classical bit, the qubit.
paras.zh: 与此同时，在量子计算领域，问题 283 可以更好地说明真正的量子问题有多么困难。科学家们了解经典计算机中的位是如何工作和操作的，但他们对量子计算与经典位的类似物——量子位——的了解较少。

paras.en: The unitary synthesis problem was first posed by researchers Scott Aaronson and Greg Kuperberg in 2006. It tries to relate working with qubits to working with bits. In this case, OpenAI showed that for any manipulation of a quantum state of qubits—called a unitary—they can build a quantum circuit and a problem dealing with only classical bits such that the circuit and problem can be used to calculate these manipulations, i.e., it can “synthesize” that unitary. Importantly, this solution gives some evidence that hard quantum problems may not be that much harder than hard classical problems, a surprising result that was not clear to researchers in the field before now.
paras.zh: 酉合成问题最初由研究人员 Scott Aaronson 和 Greg Kuperberg 于 2006 年提出。它试图将量子比特的工作与比特的工作联系起来。在这种情况下，OpenAI 表明，对于量子位的量子态（称为酉）的任何操作，他们都可以构建一个量子电路和一个仅处理经典位的问题，这样电路和问题就可以用于计算这些操作，即它可以“合成”该酉。重要的是，这个解决方案提供了一些证据，表明硬量子问题可能并不比硬经典问题难多少，这是一个令人惊讶的结果，该领域的研究人员此前并不清楚。

paras.en: The Fast Fourier Transform, an algorithm whose discovery dates back to 1965, is crucial to the Internet and other forms of digital communications. In many applications, including the Web and medical scans, it converts information received from signals into actual machine-usable frequency data. The transform works by summing a bunch of signals and multiplying each by a special exponential factor. Although brute forcing these multiplications takes quadratic time (the time is proportional to the square of the number of signals), the “fast” protocol takes about n log n time(where n is the number of signals received), which is fast enough to use for things like the Internet.
paras.zh: 快速傅里叶变换是一种算法，其发现可以追溯到 1965 年，它对于互联网和其他形式的数字通信至关重要。在许多应用中，包括网络和医疗扫描，它将从信号接收到的信息转换为实际机器可用的频率数据。该变换的工作原理是对一堆信号求和并将每个信号乘以一个特殊的指数因子。虽然暴力破解这些乘法需要二次时间（时间与信号数量的平方成正比），但“快速”协议大约需要 n log n 时间（其中 n 是接收到的信号数量），这足够快，足以用于互联网等事物。

paras.en: Paper 130 claims to reduce this n log n time to ... n (log n)0.999....Specifically, the model got it down from a factor of log n to a factor of (log n)^1–10–13, a tiny improvement over the state of the art. On an objective level, this is so close to n log n that the distinction almost doesn’t matter. It does break a longstanding barrier to digital communications, however, and many researchers hope that by studying the proof techniques used, they could one day find a Faster Fourier Transform.
paras.zh: 第 130 篇论文声称将这个 n log n 时间减少到...n (log n)0.999...具体来说，该模型将其从 log n 因子降低到 (log n)^1–10–13 因子，这比现有技术有了微小的改进。从客观角度来看，这非常接近 n log n，以至于区别几乎不重要。然而，它确实打破了数字通信的长期障碍，许多研究人员希望通过研究所使用的证明技术，他们有一天可以找到一种更快的傅里叶变换。

articles.title: The world’s loudest bird could drown out a rock concert
articles.author: Elie Dolgin

paras.en: The bare-throated bellbird is loud. Very, very loud.
paras.zh: 裸喉钟鸟的声音很大。非常非常大声。

paras.en: The explosive, metallic mating call of the snow-white male — a stout bird with a broad bill and distinctive blue-green throat patch — can top 130 decibels, louder than a jackhammer or a front-row seat at a Counting Crows concert.
paras.zh: 雪白的雄鸟——一种粗壮的鸟，有着宽阔的喙和独特的蓝绿色喉咙斑——发出爆炸性的、金属般的求偶叫声，声音可达130分贝，比手提钻或数乌鸦音乐会前排座位的声音还要大。

paras.en: That makes this South American forest dweller a contender for the title of world’s loudest bird. And now researchers think they know how it and other avian loudmouths produce such eardrum-rattling vocalizations.
paras.zh: 这使得这种南美森林居民成为世界上声音最大的鸟类称号的有力竞争者。现在研究人员认为他们知道它和其他鸟类大嘴鸟是如何发出这种震耳欲聋的声音的。

paras.en: Bigger bodies and, especially, wider beaks help these feathered screamers belt it out, behavioral ecologists João Menezes and Jeff Podos of the University of Massachusetts Amherst report September 29 in Evolution.
paras.zh: 马萨诸塞大学阿默斯特分校的行为生态学家 João Menezes 和 Jeff Podos 于 9 月 29 日在《进化论》杂志上报道称，更大的身体，尤其是更宽的喙有助于这些长有羽毛的尖叫鸟将其表达出来。

paras.en: But what pushed some birds to evolve such volume in the first place remains a mystery. The researchers looked at mating behavior, habitat density and flight ability, but found no explanation that consistently held across species. “We weren’t able to find an overarching pattern that applies to birds in general,” Menezes says.
paras.zh: 但最初是什么促使一些鸟类进化出如此大的体积仍然是一个谜。研究人员观察了交配行为、栖息地密度和飞行能力，但没有发现在不同物种之间一致成立的解释。 “我们无法找到适用于一般鸟类的总体模式，”梅内塞斯说。

paras.en: The quest to understand these sonic extremes dates back to 2019. That is when Podos and a colleague crowned the white bellbird (Procnias albus), an Amazonian cousin of the bare-throated bellbird (P. nudicollis), as a record-setting vocal powerhouse. Its 125-decibel calls were the loudest bird calls ever measured at the time.
paras.zh: 对这些声音极端现象的探索可以追溯到 2019 年。当时，波多斯和一位同事将白钟鸟 (Procnias albus)（裸喉钟鸟 (P. nudicollis) 的亚马逊近亲）评为创纪录的声音强者。它的叫声高达 125 分贝，是当时测量到的最响亮的鸟叫声。

paras.en: Beyond the attention-grabbing number, the finding raised a broader question: What makes some birds so extraordinarily loud?
paras.zh: 除了引人注目的数字之外，这一发现还提出了一个更广泛的问题：是什么让一些鸟类的声音如此之大？

paras.en: The honk of a Canada goose, for example, can reach chainsaw volume (100 decibels), while the chatter of a starling rarely rises above a dishwasher-level hum (70 decibels) — and ornithologists have surprisingly little understanding of why. Although scientists have spent decades cataloging the timing and frequency of birdsong, hoping to decode what birds are saying, the sheer loudness of bird voices has gone largely unexplored.
paras.zh: 例如，加拿大鹅的叫声可以达到电锯音量（100 分贝），而椋鸟的叫声很少会超过洗碗机级别的嗡嗡声（70 分贝）——令人惊讶的是，鸟类学家对其中的原因知之甚少。尽管科学家们花了几十年的时间对鸟鸣的时间和频率进行分类，希望能够解码鸟类所说的内容，但鸟类声音的响度在很大程度上还没有被探索过。

paras.en: To get a read on the racket, Podos lugged a high-grade sound meter, the kind used to monitor noise levels in industrial workplaces, and a laser rangefinder into the woods, swamps and open fields around his home in western Massachusetts. He measured the calls of whatever birds he could find — warblers, sparrows, robins and more.
paras.zh: 为了了解球拍情况，波多斯将一台高级声级计（用于监测工业工作场所噪音水平的那种）和一台激光测距仪拖进了他位于马萨诸塞州西部的家周围的树林、沼泽和开阔的田野。他测量了他能找到的所有鸟类的叫声——莺、麻雀、知更鸟等等。

paras.en: After logging a few dozen species, he enlisted Menezes, a then-grad student who at the time had recently joined his lab, to help turn the collection into a broader evolutionary analysis. Menezes measured bird vocalizations across his home country of Brazil, from the Atlantic Forest near São Paulo to the mountains surrounding Rio de Janeiro and beyond. He captured everything from the soft chirps of the dusky-throated hermit hummingbird to the piercing yelps of the red-legged seriema, a shaggy type of grassland bird.
paras.zh: 在记录了几十个物种后，他聘请了当时刚加入他实验室的研究生梅内塞斯来帮助将这些收集品转化为更广泛的进化分析。梅内塞斯测量了他的祖国巴西各地的鸟类发声，从圣保罗附近的大西洋森林到里约热内卢周围的山脉及更远的地方。他捕捉到了一切，从暗喉隐士蜂鸟的柔和鸣叫到红腿鸫（一种毛茸茸的草原鸟类）的刺耳叫声。

paras.en: All told, he and Podos compiled vocal volume data on 123 species, creating what they say is the largest such dataset to date.
paras.zh: 总而言之，他和 Podos 收集了 123 个物种的发声量数据，创建了他们所说的迄今为止最大的此类数据集。

paras.en: The heftier the bird, the louder its call tended to be, and the same went for birds with broader beaks — a connection between anatomy and acoustic performance that biophysicist Gabriel Mindlin from the University of Buenos Aires in Argentina finds “sensible and plausible.”
paras.zh: 鸟越重，它的叫声往往越大，对于喙部较宽的鸟来说也是如此——阿根廷布宜诺斯艾利斯大学的生物物理学家加布里埃尔·明德林认为，解剖学和声学性能之间的联系“合理且合理”。

paras.en: “Larger birds have the potential to generate greater respiratory pressures and flows, while morphological features such as beak opening can affect how efficiently acoustic energy radiates,” says Mindlin, who studies birdsong but was not involved in the work.
paras.zh: “较大的鸟类有可能产生更大的呼吸压力和流量，而喙张开等形态特征会影响声能的辐射效率，”研究鸟鸣但未参与这项工作的明德林说。

paras.en: Why evolution cranked up the volume on these avian megaphones, though, is a puzzle that remains, for now, unhatched.
paras.zh: 然而，为什么进化会提高这些鸟类扩音器的音量，目前仍然是一个尚未解开的谜团。

articles.title: ‘A Mother’s Brain’ explores the neuroscience of motherhood
articles.author: Laura Sanders

paras.en: When it comes to new motherhood, the baby typically takes center stage, garnering most of people’s attention. But in a refreshing twist, neuroscientist Susana Carmona shifts the spotlight to the mom. In the opening pages of A Mother’s Brain, Carmona cheerfully tells us, “here, we’ll hardly discuss babies at all.” Mothers are her protagonists.
paras.zh: 当谈到新妈妈时，婴儿通常占据中心舞台，吸引大多数人的注意力。但令人耳目一新的是，神经科学家苏珊娜·卡莫纳将焦点转移到了母亲身上。在《母亲的大脑》的开头几页中，卡莫纳愉快地告诉我们，“在这里，我们几乎不会讨论婴儿。”母亲是她的主角。

paras.en: What follows is a captivating, passionate and well-grounded journey through the fascinating process of “matrescence.” A word coined to echo “adolescence,” another time of seismic changes, matrescence includes the intense reorganization a woman’s brain undergoes as she becomes a mom. So far, early studies have revealed a sculpting of brain circuits (and Carmona is quick to point out that less can be more), heightened social instincts and perhaps even a boost of resilience during old age.
